topic: Design-inclusive minimax estimation of the total treatment effect under exposure-mapping ambiguity

open_problems.open_problem: What is the unavoidable adaptation penalty, relative to an oracle that knows the correct exposure mapping, for joint exact-budget design and estimation of the total treatment effect over a finite exposure-mapping ambiguity class?

source_refs.claim: Schroder et al. quantify exposure-mapping misspecification through sharp sensitivity bounds and efficient orthogonal estimation, rather than an oracle-risk comparison under chosen randomization.
source_refs.author: Maresa Schroder, Miruna Oprescu, Stefan Feuerriegel, and Nathan Kallus

source_refs.claim: No design and test can uniformly distinguish nested unrestricted exposure models, even for bounded and maximally separated alternatives.
source_refs.author: Chao Gao, Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Savje, and Yitan Wang

source_refs.claim: Borusyak, Hull, and Munro characterize the oracle design-estimator solution when the exposure operator is known.
source_refs.author: Kirill Borusyak, Peter Hull, and Evan Munro

source_refs.excerpt: Turn the higher-rank handle into a finite rank-two, three-class theorem with a proved relaxation gap
The higher-rank, noncommuting menu frontier remains open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Known-map design theory yields mapping-specific optimal assignment covariances and estimating equations, while Gao et al. show that unrestricted exposure-model identity cannot be learned uniformly from one experiment. The prior CausalSmith commitment-price proposal isolates the same obstruction geometrically: incompatible noncommuting response classes need not share an oracle direction, and its reviewer specifically asks for a proved relaxation gap. With an exact treatment budget and a nonconvex union of mapping-measurable tables, standard convex minimax interchange does not decide whether hedging costs only a constant, a slower rate, or a nonvanishing error.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be a two-sided oracle inequality or exact formula for the ratio or difference between ambiguity-robust minimax RMSE and the best mapping-specific oracle RMSE, with conditions for zero, bounded, and asymptotically positive adaptation cost and an explicit budget-feasible attaining design.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing begins with the consequences of choosing the wrong exposure compression and turns that uncertainty into a formal robustness target.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: network outcomes require treatment compression -> the analyst may choose the wrong compression -> what price must design and estimation pay to remain valid over several plausible mappings?

method_exemplars.technique: Construct mapping-specific bounded potential-outcome alternatives whose observed experiments coincide under every chosen design, giving a design-uniform minimax testing lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An adaptation lower bound needs the same indistinguishability construction, but the alternatives must be separated by oracle total-effect risk rather than only by model membership.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize the oracle assignment covariance and recentered instrument through a design-estimator minimax saddle, implement the design by Gaussian rounding, and prove a limit law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the known-mapping oracle benchmark against which the ambiguity penalty must be measured.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce worst-case design-based MSE over an ellipsoidal response class to a balance quadratic form and its minimax assignment problem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite exposure menu can induce several incompatible response geometries, so its robust risk is a simultaneous version of the same quadratic design problem.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the graph-only conservative variance envelope for heterogeneous Bernoulli bipartite experiments the exact, or uniformly constant-factor, worst-case variance over bounded fixed potential-outcome schedules?

source_refs.excerpt: Investigate whether V_env is sharp or constant-factor sharp as a worst-case bounded-outcome variance envelope
The optimality claim is envelope-optimal ... not exact minimax optimality for the true design variance

open_problems.why_unsolved: The envelope is obtained by absolute-value domination of outcome-dependent covariance terms. It is observable and design-optimizable, but no least-favourable bounded schedule is known to align every covariance sign while also satisfying the required centering restrictions. Consequently, minimizing the envelope does not yet imply minimax optimality for the causal estimator, and the reviewer explicitly identified sharpness or a universal factor as the missing strengthening.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be a sharpness theorem constructing least-favourable bounded potential outcomes for every graph and design, or a counterexample family together with the optimal universal approximation factor and an attaining design.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the nearest design-based bipartite Hajek setup and variance motivation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: bipartite interference requires exposure-weighted Hajek inference -> heterogeneous probabilities can improve precision -> decide whether the optimized graph-only envelope is the true minimax causal risk

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize a network design against finite-sample estimator variance and prove oracle-regret control by comparing feasible designs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The missing result is a genuine design-and-estimator risk comparison rather than optimality for a convex surrogate alone.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent conservative interference variance bounds as convex programs and prove their validity from admissible quadratic domination.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The open question asks when precisely such a conservative quadratic envelope is sharp for the underlying causal variance.

open_problems.open_problem: Under an exact treated-count budget, what is the realizable assignment-covariance slice and the exact zero-versus-positive implementability-loss frontier for the two-block interference-homophily design objective?

source_refs.excerpt: Scoped out of v1: graph families beyond two-block, the fixed-treatment-count design class

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked covariance-image theorem uses sign-symmetric Bernoulli margins and a parity-truncated cut-polytope slice. Fixing the number treated imposes a global cardinality constraint that changes both the realizable covariance geometry and the SDP rounding argument; the proposal explicitly records the fixed-count class as a different geometry, not a routine restriction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be an explicit characterization of the fixed-cardinality covariance image, followed by an iff phase boundary and a sharp formula for the constrained-versus-relaxed causal-MSE loss.

writing_exemplar.why: Its interference-homophily robustness objective supplies the design criterion whose exact-budget geometry remains unresolved.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: graph-aware worst-case MSE yields a covariance SDP -> an SDP covariance need not be an assignment law -> determine exact attainability when assignments also obey a treatment budget

method_exemplars.technique: Identify realizable Bernoulli correlation matrices as an affine cut-polytope image and prove necessity and sufficiency geometrically.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The first required object is exactly the covariance image of a constrained assignment-law class.

method_exemplars.technique: Use SDP hierarchies and cardinality-preserving rounding with proof control of objective loss under a global count constraint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The exact treated-count restriction is the global-cardinality obstruction absent from the Bernoulli-margin covariance result.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the finite-sample minimax RMSE for the all-treated-versus-all-control total treatment effect when the experimenter jointly chooses any exact-budget assignment design and estimator but the fixed potential-outcome table is measurable under an unknown member of a finite exposure-mapping class?

source_refs.claim: Viviano optimizes a prespecified linear estimator under a known local exposure model and explicitly leaves alternative exposure mappings and broader interaction structures open.
source_refs.author: Davide Viviano

source_refs.claim: The paper takes the infimum over design and test and proves minimax impossibility for exposure-model specification testing, but its loss is testing error for a separation functional rather than estimation risk for a causal contrast.
source_refs.author: Chao Gao, Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Savje, and Yitan Wang

source_refs.claim: The paper gives sharp sensitivity bounds and efficient orthogonal estimators under exposure-mapping misspecification, with the observed-data regime held fixed rather than optimized over designs.
source_refs.author: Maresa Schroder, Miruna Oprescu, Stefan Feuerriegel, and Nathan Kallus

source_refs.claim: The paper jointly optimizes assignment and a recentered-IV estimator for worst-case asymptotic variance, assuming a known exposure mapping and a linear spillover model.
source_refs.author: Kirill Borusyak, Peter Hull, and Evan Munro

source_refs.claim: The paper derives minimax rates over designs and linear estimators for the global effect when interference decays with distance, leaving finite exposure-model ambiguity outside its class.
source_refs.author: Stefan Faridani and Paul Niehaus

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest papers optimize different losses or impose assumptions that remove the ambiguity: Gao et al. study testing loss; Schroder et al. study sharp bounds in a fixed observational regime; Borusyak, Hull, and Munro solve a design-estimator saddle only for a known linear exposure operator; and Faridani and Niehaus assume distance decay. A finite union of mapping-measurable fixed-outcome models is nonconvex, while the exact treatment budget excludes the endpoint assignments defining the target, so neither exposure-probability weighting nor known-model minimax duality yields a converse valid for every design and estimator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be an explicit graph-, budget-, and ambiguity-class functional giving a universal finite-sample minimax RMSE lower bound, together with a budget-feasible design and estimator attaining it up to a universal constant.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from network interference to variance-optimal design and ends by naming alternative exposure mappings as an open design question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: network interference makes conventional randomization imprecise -> design can exploit a known local exposure mapping -> how should design and estimation change when the exposure mapping itself is ambiguous?

method_exemplars.technique: Form a joint design-estimator minimax problem, dualize the worst-case second-moment objective, solve a relaxed covariance design, and implement it by Gaussian rounding with recentered-IV limit theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest design-and-analysis saddle; the missing step is replacing its known linear exposure operator by the nonconvex union induced by ambiguity.

method_exemplars.technique: Pair a least-favourable lower bound over designs with cluster-scale constructions, IPW or de-weighted OLS estimators, bandwidth selection, and inference for the global treatment contrast.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It targets the same all-treated-versus-none contrast and optimizes designs and estimators, but its structure is spatial decay rather than finite exposure-map ambiguity.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct design-uniform indistinguishable bounded potential-outcome alternatives after taking the infimum over experimental designs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its least-favourable construction already survives endogenous design choice and must be redirected from model separation to separation in the total-effect functional.

open_problems.open_problem: Which graph-, budget-, and exposure-class conditions make total-effect estimation design-remediable, and which force a positive asymptotic minimax error, when exposure mappings may be nonlocal?

source_refs.claim: Basse and Airoldi prove that under arbitrary interference even structural assumptions permitting unbiased estimation need not make variance vanish asymptotically.
source_refs.author: Guillaume W. Basse and Edoardo M. Airoldi

source_refs.claim: The conflict-graph design turns target-specific unobservability under a known arbitrary-neighborhood exposure model into an estimator variance bound controlled by the conflict graph's spectral radius.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Charilaos Pipis, Constantinos Daskalakis, and Christopher Harshaw

source_refs.claim: The design-based Riesz framework gives necessary and sufficient estimability conditions for a linear causal functional relative to a specified potential-outcome function space and design.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Savje, and Yitan Wang

source_refs.claim: Exposure-model correctness cannot be uniformly tested from one randomized experiment without restrictions beyond discrete exposure mappings, regardless of design.
source_refs.author: Chao Gao, Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Savje, and Yitan Wang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature identifies opposite endpoints but not the frontier: arbitrary interference can make global effects nonconcentrating, while a known neighborhood model admits conflict-graph designs with spectral rates. For a finite class of possibly nonlocal mappings, each mapping induces a different endpoint-exposure collision and observability relation on the exact-budget assignment slice. Taking their union can destroy both the single-model conflict graph and the linear function-space structure used by Riesz representation, leaving no existing criterion for when design choice covers the competing endpoint exposures well enough for consistency.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be a sufficient-condition classification through an explicit exposure-conflict or coverage functional, proving consistency when it vanishes and a positive minimax lower bound when it stays bounded away from zero, with concrete nonempty examples of both regimes and no claim of exhaustive necessity.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames experimental design around target-specific unobservability and converts that obstruction into a graph object controlling achievable precision.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: network causal targets create incompatible exposure events -> a conflict graph records their unobservability -> what replaces that graph, and what frontier follows, under a finite ambiguity class?

method_exemplars.technique: Encode incompatible target-exposure events as a conflict graph, randomize using a graph-aware design, and control a modified Horvitz-Thompson estimator through the graph spectral radius.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired classification likewise needs a combinatorial object connecting endpoint observability to design geometry, now simultaneously across several mappings.

method_exemplars.technique: Use design-based Riesz representers to characterize unbiasedness and consistency, then derive asymptotic normality and conservative variance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: For each exposure model, endpoint effects are linear functionals on a mapping-specific space; the frontier must determine when a common or robust representer exists across their union.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct potential-outcome schedules that remain observationally indistinguishable or nonconcentrating under design-based sampling despite structural restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These constructions give the negative-regime template for proving that specified ambiguity and budget geometries are design-inert.

literature_map:
Gao, Harshaw, Savje, and Wang (2026, arXiv:2605.09726) prove design-inclusive minimax impossibility for testing unrestricted discrete exposure models, not causal-contrast estimation.
Schroder, Oprescu, Feuerriegel, and Kallus (2026, arXiv:2602.03459) derive sharp exposure-misspecification bounds and efficient orthogonal estimators in a fixed observational regime.
Borusyak, Hull, and Munro (2026, arXiv:2607.18601) solve a joint design-estimator worst-case variance problem for known linear exposure mappings and recentered IV.
Viviano (2026 revision, arXiv:2003.08421) optimizes two-wave network experiments under known local exposure and explicitly names alternative mappings and broader propagation as open.
Faridani and Niehaus (2024, revised 2026, NBER 33319/arXiv:2209.14181) obtain minimax design-estimator rates for the global effect under distance-decaying interference.
Thiyageswaran et al. (2026, arXiv:2601.17145) optimize worst-case MSE for a fixed Horvitz-Thompson estimator under a specified interference-homophily model via SDP and vector balancing.
Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw (2024, arXiv:2411.10908) introduce a target-specific conflict graph and obtain spectral-rate designs under known arbitrary neighborhood interference.
Leung (2022, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/22-AOS2224) proves near-rate-optimal cluster designs, asymptotic normality, and variance estimation under spatial decay.
Harshaw et al. (2023, Electronic Journal of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/23-EJS2111) estimate the total effect in bipartite experiments under a known linear exposure-response model.
Harshaw, Savje, and Wang (2025 revision, arXiv:2210.08698) give Riesz-based necessary and sufficient estimability conditions for general design-based functionals.
Savje (2024, Biometrika, DOI:10.1093/biomet/asad019) separates exposure-defined estimands from correct exposure-model assumptions but does not optimize designs over a finite model union.
Savje, Aronow, and Hudgens (2021, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/20-AOS1973) obtain consistency for a design-dependent expected ATE under limited unknown interference, while distinguishing it from the global all-versus-none effect.
Basse and Airoldi (2018, Sociological Methodology, DOI:10.1177/0081175018782569) show arbitrary interference can preclude concentration even when unbiased estimators exist.
Aronow and Samii (2017, Annals of Applied Statistics, DOI:10.1214/16-AOAS1005) establish the canonical design-exposure-estimand framework and exposure-probability weighting under a specified mapping.
Hudgens and Halloran (2008, JASA, DOI:10.1198/016214508000000292) provide foundational finite-population direct, indirect, total, and overall effects under partial interference.
Harshaw, Middleton, and Savje (2026, JASA, DOI:10.1080/01621459.2026.2627027) optimize conservative design-based variance bounds when exact variance is unidentifiable under interference.
